newsitem.title: USA: Tobacco shares dip further as investors keep clear.
newsitem.headline: Tobacco shares dip further as investors keep clear.

text.p: U.S. tobacco stocks extended their decline on Friday as investors wary over the potential impact of anti-tobacco litigation steered clear of the group.
"There's an awful lot of smoke that has to clear before I think you take a major stance here," said Frank Calta, director of trading at Anvil Institutional Services.
Group leader Philip Morris Cos Inc fell 3-3/4 to 112, RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp gave back 5/8 to 30-7/8 and Loews Corp sank two to 96-1/2.
The American Stock Exchange's Tobacco Index stumbled 3-1/2 points to 280, a drop of 1.2 percent.
The index, launched in early March, is off 12.5 percent from its high of 320.

The group was hit Thursday by the most serious blow yet to the cigarette industry. Liggett Group, the smallest U.S. tobacco company and a unit of Brooke Group Ltd, agreed to settle tobacco litigation with attorneys general from 22 states and give up potentially damaging documents.
Tobacco industry analysts said they expected the stocks to rebound from the latest setback on the legal front.
But some on Wall Street remained wary.

Tobacco stocks "have had big moves over the last two years, and people believed that they had discounted all the negatives," said Phil Roth, chief technical analyst at Dean Witter Reynolds. "Clearly, they haven't. This is a controversial group with relentless bad press. That's why I don't like these stocks even if they are cheap."
While cigarette makers floundered, one maker of an alternative was shining. Caribbean Cigar Inc rose 11/16 to 8-1/2.
